description.summary: desktop shell control of compositor state

protocol.description: Compositor features a desktop shell configures that no standard protocol covers. Only unsandboxed clients see these globals. Outputs are named by their connector, as in zwlr_output_head_v1.name.

interface.name: dsk_output_manager_v1
interface.description: Mirroring an output removes it from the desktop and shows another output's frames on it, scaled to fit. Mode, scale, position, and enablement stay on zwlr_output_manager_v1. The compositor persists mirror changes.

request.name: set_mirror
request.description: The result arrives as a mirror or failed event for target.

request.name: set_property
request.description: Properties zwlr_output_manager_v1 does not carry, named by their [output] config keys: "vrr" (disabled, always, fullscreen), "hdr" (off, on, auto, fullscreen), "sdr_white" (80 to 1000), "tearing", "workspaces" (dynamic or a count from 1 to 64), "min_workspaces", "cyclic_workspaces", and "workspace_axis" (vertical, horizontal). An empty value removes the saved key. Saved in displays.toml under the display's descriptor. Answered by property events and done, or by failed.

event.name: property

description.summary: effective value of one display property

event.description: Sent for every output and property on bind and after every configuration change, followed by done.

event.name: mirror
event.description: Sent for every connected output on bind, and for an output whenever its mirror state changes. An empty source means not mirroring.

description.summary: end of the initial state batch

event.name: failed
event.description: Unknown output, a source that is itself a mirror, or target equal to source.

interface.name: dsk_settings_manager_v1
interface.description: Every compositor setting a settings app may change: input, appearance, animation, layout, workspaces, overview, and focus. Settings are named by their config keys ("input.touchpad.tap", "appearance.border_width"), with values as plain text ("true", "0.3", "adaptive", "us,de"). An empty value means unset, which restores the value from the user's config files or the built-in default. The compositor validates, applies, and persists every change in its settings file, which it loads after the user's config files, so a change made here always takes effect.

request.name: set
request.description: Answered by setting events and done, or by failed.

request.name: bind
request.description: Binds chord (as the config file writes it: "Mod+Shift+q", "submap[resize],Escape") to action ("window-close", "spawn:foot"), stored in the settings file. An empty action removes the settings file's entry, so the user's config files or the built-in set apply again; the action "none" unbinds the chord. Answered by keybind events and done, or by failed with the chord as key.

request.name: capture_chord
request.description: The next key press, with its modifiers, is reported by chord_captured instead of reaching keybinds or any client, so a chord that is already bound can be recorded. Escape with no modifiers cancels. Ends when the object is destroyed.

event.name: device_added
event.description: Sent for every connected device on bind and whenever one connects.

event.name: setting
event.description: Sent for every setting on bind and after every configuration change. customized is 1 when the settings file holds a value for the key, so setting it to the empty value changes what applies.

event.name: keybind
event.description: Sent for every keybind on bind and after every configuration change, in the syntax the bind request takes. customized is 1 when the settings file sets the chord. A chord the settings file unbinds is sent with the action "none".

event.name: action_spec
event.description: Sent once per action on bind. param is empty for an action without an argument, otherwise a hint such as "<cmd>".

event.name: chord_captured
event.description: Answers capture_chord. Empty when the capture was cancelled.

description.summary: end of a batch of events

interface.name: dsk_shell_v1
interface.description: Bound by the desktop shell. Keybinds that drive the shell arrive as action events on the connection the shell already holds, so no process is started per keypress. The compositor also reports the keyboard lock-key state it owns, so the shell never polls LEDs.

event.name: action
event.description: A command line in the shell's own command language, as typed after the shell's IPC verb, for example "panel-toggle launcher".

event.name: lock_keys
event.description: Sent on bind and whenever the state changes. Each argument is 1 when that lock is active and 0 otherwise.

event.name: bell

description.summary: an app rang the system bell

event.description: A client rang xdg_system_bell_v1. The shell alerts the user the way its sound settings say. app_id names the ringing window's app, or is empty when the bell came without a surface.
